I will broadcast half a bag of urea on this plot, just like last season, because the soil here is tired and the rice needs strength to grow. I also hauled two cartloads of cow manure here — it is heavy work but it costs no shillings, and the landlord expects to see a good field. I am planting the seed I kept from my last harvest; I do not know these new seeds the agro-dealer talks about, and I have no extra cash to waste on something I have not seen grow. My wife and children will work with me to weed and harvest, and if the rice comes well I will hire two young men for two days each to help with the threshing.
